Beer’s potential effects on lactation are contested. Some sources report that polysaccharides in beer (barley and hops) may transiently raise prolactin, a hormone linked to milk production, but authoritative guidance notes alcohol itself decreases milk production and recommends avoiding alcohol while breastfeeding [d1,d2,d5,d6]. Survey data suggest a subset of mothers perceive increased supply after drinking beer, yet controlled studies in nursing mothers are lacking [d2,d5]. Historical and cultural sources promote beer as a galactagogue, but these claims lack robust scientific backing [d4]. Overall, the evidence base is mixed and does not support recommending beer to improve lactation [d1,d2,d3,d5,d6].
